messages:
maria: Starting a thread — proposal for making KV cache keys architecture- and seqlen-aware + durable across driver restarts. TL;DR: per-arch salt + seqlen-bucketing + versioned namespace, persisted to RocksDB with a tiny journal for fast recovery.

dan: +1 on per-arch salt. we saw wrong kernel lookups when the same model was served on nv50 vs nv60 in last canary.

oliver: quick question: why RocksDB vs LMDB or simple mmap?

maria: RocksDB for write throughput + compaction controls; we need a GC friendly store since keys get churny with short-lived prefixes. LMDB didn't handle burst writes well in my local perf tests.

sara: can you share key format? need to make sure it fits existing cache APIs.

maria: proposed key format (pseudo):
```
key = join("|", [namespace_v, arch_salt, model_id, model_version, seqlen_bucket, prefix_hash])
// example: v3|a1b2|gptx-7b|r3|seq-32|3f4c2d
```

lee: seqlen_bucket is interesting — how wide are buckets? do we risk explosion?

maria: start with coarse bins: 1-32,33-128,129-512,513+; we can refine based on observed distribution. buckets only change kernel selection if above thresholds, so not too many buckets.

dan: persistence + driver restarts: how to avoid stale keys when kernel ABI changes? need a driver build id in namespace.

maria: exactly. namespace_v = concat(platform_rollout_tag, cache_schema_v). increment on driver/runtime/model rollout that affects kernel layout. ops-bot: @infra-bot triggered rollout check: current driver build 2026.03.10-rc14, cache_schema_v=3.

infra-bot: noted — will emit a :warning: if schema bump happens during canary.

oliver: perf numbers? did this actually help hit-rates and latency?

maria: quick summary from yesterday's staging run (mixed traffic replay):
- baseline (no arch salt / no seqlen): cache hit 41%, p50 latency 34ms
- with arch salt + seq buckets + persisted store: hit 64%, p50 latency 20ms, p95 improved ~22%
These are rough but consistent across 3 runs.

sara: how do we handle model rollouts where we do gradual canary? keys must not invalidate the entire cache and warm-up should be graceful.

maria: approach: namespace_v includes model_version tag; for canary we write new keys under new namespace but leave old keys intact. routing policy routes e.g., 5% to new namespace until stable. After cutoff we garbage collect old namespaces based on retention TTL.

lee: GC plan? immediate deletes are risky. we need safe TTLs + manual triggers for storage reclamation.

maria: propose retention policy: keep last N namespaces per model (N=3), and soft TTL 72h after last route traffic; manual compaction option for emergencies.

dan: any concern about key explosion due to many combos (arch x seqlen x model versions)?

maria: mitigations: prefix dedupe (store prefix hash only), compact small buckets, and a bloom filter per namespace to cheaply check membership. plus periodic eviction by LRU tuned per workload.

ops-bot: perf test command for repro:
```bash
./tools/replay_traffic --trace replay.json --enable-arch-salt --seq-buckets --persist-store=rocksdb --db-path=/tmp/kvdb_test
```

infra-bot: running quick health check on /tmp/kvdb_test usage now.

oliver: what about cross-architecture migrations? if model moves from nv50->nv60, old keys become useless but we still want warmup. maybe a background copy of hot keys with remapping?

maria: background hot-key promotion: periodically sample top-K hot prefixes and re-hash them into new arch namespace to pre-warm new runtime. cost limited to top-K to bound IO.

sara: any eval for correctness/regressions? we saw earlier a bug where seqlen binning changed kernel choice but didn't update kv meta and caused mismatch.

maria: fixed in autotuner: kernel decision stored with key metadata version; on lookup we assert-compatible(kernel_meta, runtime_kernel_capabilities) and fallback to compute path if mismatch. added unit + integration test.

dan: rollout plan? sounds good but needs canary, perf guardrails, and a rollback path.

maria: rollout plan draft: 1) staging run (done), 2) internal canary on dedicated pools (10%), monitor hit-rate + p95 token latency + token/sec, 3) expand to 50% if stable, 4) full rollout with delayed GC. metrics thresholds: no more than 5% regression in p95 or less than 3% increase in token-cost per 1k.

lee: who owns upgrade script for namespace bumps?

maria: infra team + runtime. I'll open a PR with the bump tool.

ops-bot: reminder: add migration alert to runbook: "namespace schema bump — check leaked keys + run compaction"

infra-bot: logging note: include namespace_v and arch_salt in every cache-miss log to help postmortem.

oliver: anything else wrt batching heuristics? seqlen-aware batching could cooperate with keying (same seqlen bin => higher coalescing).

maria: yes — plan to pass seqlen_bucket tag to the router so it co-batches similar bins. small patch ready, will send for review.

sara: ack. can we get a simple dashboard showing per-namespace hit-rate and hot-prefix counts? that'll help during canary.

maria: adding dashboard to Redwood Console draft. I also attached a short CSV of staging runs to the PR.

dan: thanks — this looks actionable. small nit: document where to find retention/compaction knobs.

maria: noted, will update the RFC. :thumbsup:
